context.title: The Light of the World
context.summary: A woman caught in adultery is brought to Jesus, and he sends away her accusers. In the temple he calls himself the light of the world, debates who are Abraham's true children, and declares, 'Before Abraham was, I am.'
context.background: The story of the woman (7:53–8:11) is missing from the earliest manuscripts and appears in different places in later ones; many scholars think it is a genuine early story added to John later. During Tabernacles, great lamps lit the temple's Court of Women, near the treasury where Jesus spoke (v. 20).

customs.note: The law named death for both the man and the woman (Leviticus 20:10; Deuteronomy 22:22). Bringing only the woman exposes the trap.

watchFor: 'He that is without sin among you, let him first cast a stone' (v. 7).
'I am' (v. 58) echoes God's name to Moses, and hearers pick up stones.

people.name: Jesus
people.also: Immanuel, Emmanuel, Messiah, Shiloh, Christ, Jesus Christ, Messias
people.summary: Anointed, the Greek translation of the Hebrew word rendered “Messiah”, the official title of our Lord, occurring five hundred and fourteen times in the New Testament.

people.name: Moses
people.summary: Drawn (or Egypt. mesu, “son;” hence Rameses, royal son). On the invitation of Pharaoh (Gen. 45:17-25), Jacob and his sons went down into Egypt.

people.name: Abraham
people.summary: Father of a multitude, son of Terah, named (Gen. 11:27) before his older brothers Nahor and Haran, because he was the heir of the promises. Till the age of seventy, Abram sojourned among his kindred in his native country of Chaldea.

places.name: mount of Olives
places.summary: So called from the olive trees with which its sides are clothed, is a mountain ridge on the east of Jerusalem (1 Kings 11:7; Ezek. 11:23; Zech. 14:4), from which it is separated by the valley of Kidron.
